samples.summary: Design doc claims an unturned-on reader gets "none of the per-edit bookkeeping", but attribution writes are unconditional. `YorkieNoteStore.editText` always attaches `{a, t}` to every inserted run regardless of the `showAuthors` preference (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts), so every user pays the CRDT/wire cost of the feature even if nobody in the workspace ever enables the gutter. This is arguably the right design (attribution must accrue for the gutter to be useful later), but the doc's "nothing changes for someone who never turns it on" framing — repeated in the task doc's acceptance criterion — overstates it and should say so explicitly (off = no layout/gutter change, but writes are always attributed).
samples.evidence: notes.md:516-518 "off by default ... none of the per-edit bookkeeping" vs unconditional `root.content.edit(..., {a,t})` in editText.

samples.summary: Scope creep beyond issue #814: the peer caret label path is changed too. The task doc's acceptance criteria and file list (docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-blame-gutter-todo.md:9-42) cover the blame gutter only; sanitizing `peer.name` in `remote-selection.ts` alters pre-existing collaboration rendering (a peer name is now stripped/capped at 64 chars) and adds a test for it. Defensible as sharing one boundary, but it is unrequested behaviour change riding along with a reading-aid feature and would be better as its own change.
samples.evidence: remote-selection.ts now wraps NoteCaretWidget name with sanitizeDisplayName; not in the todo's file list.

samples.summary: `sanitizeDisplayName` is placed in `@wafflebase/notes`, but the identical problem (rendering an unverified peer presence `name` to the DOM/canvas) already exists in the docs and slides peer-presence renderers (`packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:446`, `packages/slides/src/view/editor/overlay.ts:162`). Repo convention is that cross-editor shared code lives in `@wafflebase/core`; putting the sanitizer in the notes engine means the other editors either duplicate it later or stay unhardened.
samples.evidence: No sanitizer found in packages/core; docs/slides render presence names unsanitized.

samples.summary: The share-link note view mounts `NotesView` with no toolbar and no `showAuthors` prop, so a share-link editor/viewer can never turn the gutter on even though their own edits are being attributed. The acceptance criterion says the feature is toggled "from the view menu"; the shared surface has none. Probably intentional (the shared view has no view menu at all today), but worth confirming against the issue.

The "Show authors" checkbox is added to the view-mode dropdown, which is rendered even when the note is in preview-only (`viewMode: "view"`) or read-only mode. In those states the gutter has no editor to attach to, so toggling the item changes a persisted preference with no visible effect. A disabled/hidden item when `mode === 'view'` would fit the menu's existing semantics better.
samples.evidence: notes-toolbar.tsx:329-367 — the view dropdown is outside the `!readOnly` guard and unconditional on `mode`.

samples.summary: Retention/growth is recorded as "deliberately unbounded for now", but a per-keystroke `t: Date.now()` guarantees adjacent runs can never merge, so the note's run count (and the `getAuthorSpans()` walk performed on every doc change while the gutter is on) grows monotonically with edit count for the life of the note, with no compaction path sketched. Coarsening `t` (e.g. bucket to the minute) so runs by one author merge would keep the same UX at a fraction of the cost; at minimum the doc should name that as the mitigation rather than leaving the open question unbounded.
samples.evidence: notes.md:545-550 storage note; yorkie-note-store.ts writes `t: Date.now()` per insert.
